doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Parents never saw him in nightclubs; father and the movie house car
summary: His parents refused to enter nightclubs; his father wouldn't enter a movie house to claim a car.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well let me just pick up — was it a point of conversation in your family that Jon is working in a nightclub?

Oh, yeah, Jonny was able to earn money in a nightclub. My father never saw me. My mother never saw me, because they sold liquor in nightclubs and they would never go. But I sang at banquets at times and they would come and they would see me. But my father won a car in the 30s when nobody had a car, and wouldn’t go into the movie house to get the car, because that is forbidden in the Bible.
I’m not following you on that.

Well places of amusement are forbidden for the followers of the Word to go to. So in order to get the car he had to go there and present the ticket, and he wouldn’t go, he would not do it, he would not go. And one of my brothers was older, 22 or something, he © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-
says, “that’s stupid.” And my father knocked him down. He said, “get upstairs and go to bed,” he says, “I’m a grown man,” and he says, “you’re in my house.”
I guess he had his priorities in order.
